newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher despite profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher despite profit-taking.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed higher, but off from opening peaks, in hectic trade on Wednesday due to an easing of worries that the central bank may launch measures to curb the market's recent wild gains, brokers said.
The weighted index ended 14.82 points or 0.19 percent higher at 7,656.85.
Turnover was a frantic T$156.99 billion. That surpassed the T$152.13 billion total set on January 7, 1994, and marked the highest turnover since T$185.9 billion on January 6, 1994.
Earlier in the session the index had soared to an intra-day high of 7,762.38.
But late profit-taking erased much of the gains, brokers said.

"The huge turnover increased profit-taking pressure in the second half session because many investors became concerned that buying interest may have capped," said Ben Lee, senior analyst for Nomura Securities.
Central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said recently that the market had "risen slightly too much", triggering a mild sell-off on Tuesday.
"But the market was no longer concerned about that, as the central bank has not tried to affect trading," Lee said.
Electronics led gainers on Wednesday, rising 1.75 percent with Mustek Systems soaring by the daily seven-percent limit or T$10 to close at T$155.
But plastics suffered from profit-taking, losing 1.96 percent. Formosa Plastics fell 3.38 percent or T$2.50 to T$71.50.
Brokers said the market largely ignored lingering rumours that China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping's health was worsening. "Deng's health was not a factor today," Lee said.
Brokers expected the index to consolidate at the current level. A 7,600-7,700 range was seen for Thursday.
